messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Orbit (enterprise-vpc-us-east) elevated error rate >30% and 5xx spikes, started 2026-03-15T16:05Z. Paging oncall

tara: I'm on it. Looking at logs now. Can someone confirm if this is dedicated pool or shared?

jordan: It's Orbit's dedicated pool in us-east-1 (dedicated-orbit-us-east). We saw degraded health after provider maintenance ~15:50Z; a subset of GPUs never came back up.

matt: Confirmed — warm pool exists in us-west-2 (dedicated-orbit-us-west, 4 warm nodes). Current routing policy is weighted DNS (Route53). TTL is 60s.

tara: OK plan: 1) notify customer + PS/contact 2) move 10% traffic to us-west for canary 3) monitor for 2m, then shift remaining 90% if stable. Need DNS change doc and ops approval.

ana: (support_ana) I've opened a CS ticket and pinged Orbit SRE lead. Status page prepped. Will post an update when we start the canary.

jordan: I prepared Route53 change-batch payload. Example file (failover-canary.json):

```json
{
  "Comment": "Orbit failover canary - shift 10% to us-west-2",
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "UPSERT",
      "ResourceRecordSet": {
        "Name": "orbit.api.redwood.example.com.",
        "Type": "A",
        "SetIdentifier": "us-west-2-canary",
        "Weight": 10,
        "TTL": 60,
        "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "3.120.45.22"}]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

jordan: Command to execute: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z0123456 --change-batch file://failover-canary.json`

matt: I confirm backend readiness in us-west: all warm nodes passed health checks, KV caches primed, model variants loaded. Latency target should hold.

ryan: Logging/metrics — watch these dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/orbit/tenant-health and the error-rate panel. I'll take the metrics watch.

tara: Executing canary now. tagging this thread with `incident:orbit-failover`. Ana — go ahead and post initial customer note: "We are shifting a small percentage of traffic to a warm standby in another region to reduce errors."

ops-bot: change-resource-record-sets request accepted. Change ID: CAA123EXAMPLE. Status: PENDING.

jordan: Change propagated; I see the weighted record active. Canaries at 10% starting 16:12Z.

ryan: 16:14Z metrics: errors down to 12% overall, us-west both healthy, request latency stable. Continuing 2m window.

matt: Good signal. Proceeding to ramp to 100% by updating weight to 100 and deprecating us-east record. Will schedule 3-step ramp: 30% -> 70% -> 100% with 60s pauses.

jordan: Rolling first step to 30% now.

ryan: 16:18Z errors down to 4%, us-east still returning some 5xx but low traffic. No downstream alerts.

ops-bot: change-resource-record-sets request accepted. Change ID: CAA124EXAMPLE.

matt: 70% now.

ryan: 16:20Z - post-handoff note: tara handing oncall to jordan for remainder of incident. 

tara: Handoff done — leaving monitoring to jordan and ryan. I updated the incident doc with timeline and actions.

jordan: 100% now. Finalizing DNS: removing us-east weighted entry and making us-west primary.

ops-bot: change-resource-record-sets request accepted. Change ID: CAA125EXAMPLE.

ryan: 16:27Z metrics: error rate back to baseline ~0.3%, latency within SLO. Active connections stable.

ana: Customer update sent: "Traffic successfully routed to warm region; we expect no further impact. We'll follow up with a root cause and timeline."

liz: Quick note for postmortem: we should validate provider maintenance hooks for GPU lifecycle and add automation to reattach failed GPUs into warm pools faster.

jordan: Agreed — capturing RCA tasks in the incident doc. Closing the P1 monitoring window; will keep a 1hr watch.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated -> monitoring. P1 -> P2 (monitoring).

jordan: Final check at 17:04Z: all systems green, no customer-facing errors. I'll schedule the postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 PT and assign owners.

ops-bot: Incident auto-archive scheduled in 7 days.

ryan: Thanks team.
